es: Producir un mensaje de voz para un amigo con bloques de sentido marcados, palabras clave acentuadas y formas reducidas, y valorar qué registro transmite cada versión.

teaching.en: A short pause after each chunk gives the listener time to take in your message, especially when it includes numbers.
teaching.es: Una pausa breve tras cada bloque da al oyente tiempo para asimilar tu mensaje, sobre todo si incluye cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Cada chunk es una idea completa; la pausa se marca con una barra (/).
segments: A short pause after each chunk gives the listener time
to take in your message, especially when it includes numbers.
teaching.audioText: A short pause after each chunk gives the listener time to take in your message, especially when it includes numbers.

teaching.en: The key words, such as the time, the place and the price, carry the stress, while weak words like 'to' and 'the' are said quickly.
teaching.es: Las palabras clave, como la hora, el lugar y el precio, llevan el acento, mientras que las palabras débiles como «to» y «the» se dicen rápido.
teaching.explanationEs: Acentúa la información importante; las palabras gramaticales se debilitan.
segments: The key words, such as the time, the place and the price, carry
the stress, while weak words like 'to' and 'the' are said quickly.
teaching.audioText: The key words, such as the time, the place and the price, carry the stress, while weak words like 'to' and 'the' are said quickly.

teaching.en: If you rehearse and run through your message once aloud, you will notice where your voice starts to trail off and where a pause would sound more natural.
teaching.es: Si ensayas y repasas tu mensaje una vez en voz alta, notarás dónde se apaga tu voz y dónde una pausa sonaría más natural.
teaching.explanationEs: Rehearse = ensayar; run through = repasar de principio a fin; trail off = apagarse la voz.
segments: If you rehearse and run through your message once aloud, you will notice where
your voice starts to trail off and where a pause would sound more natural.
teaching.audioText: If you rehearse and run through your message once aloud, you will notice where your voice starts to trail off and where a pause would sound more natural.

teaching.en: You can emphasise a number to correct a misunderstanding, as in 'I said NINE, not five, so please don't be late.'
teaching.es: Puedes enfatizar una cifra para corregir un malentendido, como en «Dije NUEVE, no cinco, así que no llegues tarde».
teaching.explanationEs: Emphasise significa dar más fuerza a una palabra para aclarar o corregir.
segments: You can emphasise a number to correct a misunderstanding, as in
'I said NINE, not five, so please don't be late.'
teaching.audioText: You can emphasise a number to correct a misunderstanding, as in 'I said NINE, not five, so please don't be late.'

teaching.en: English rhythm comes from stressed syllables arriving at roughly regular intervals, so the weak words between them get squeezed together.
teaching.es: El ritmo del inglés nace de sílabas acentuadas que llegan a intervalos más o menos regulares, así que las palabras débiles entre ellas se comprimen.
teaching.explanationEs: El ritmo depende de los acentos, no de cada sílaba.
segments: English rhythm comes from stressed syllables arriving at roughly regular
intervals, so the weak words between them get squeezed together.
teaching.audioText: English rhythm comes from stressed syllables arriving at roughly regular intervals, so the weak words between them get squeezed together.

teaching.en: A good voice note has a clear cadence: a steady pace, a pause after each chunk, and a slightly higher voice on the key information, so slow down when you reach the numbers.
teaching.es: Una buena nota de voz tiene una cadencia clara: un ritmo constante, una pausa tras cada bloque y una voz algo más aguda en la información clave, así que habla más despacio al llegar a las cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Cadence es la melodía del mensaje; slow down (hablar más despacio) ayuda si te precipitas.
segments: A good voice note has a clear cadence: a steady pace, a pause after each chunk, and
a slightly higher voice on the key information, so slow down when you reach the numbers.

prompt.es: Elige la versión que divide el mensaje en bloques de sentido claros.

choices.text: Hi Leo, it's Mia, I'm gonna / be late because the train / is delayed so please start / without me.
Hi Leo, / it's Mia, / I'm gonna be late / because the train is delayed / so please start without me.
Hi Leo, it's Mia, / I'm gonna be / late because the train is / delayed so please start without me.

feedback.es: Cada bloque es una idea completa: saludo, identificación, problema, razón y petición; las otras versiones cortan a mitad de idea.

hint.es: Cada pausa debe cerrar una idea completa, no cortarla por la mitad.

origin.text: Draft: Hi Leo, it's Mia, I'm gonna be late because the train is delayed so please start without me.

prompt.es: Completa: cada bloque termina con una pausa breve.

feedback.es: La pausa tras cada bloque da tiempo al oyente para asimilar la información.

hint.es: Se marca con una barra (/) en el guion escrito.

origin.text: Good voice messages are divided into short chunks. Each one ends with a ___, which gives the listener a moment to take in the information.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Avísame si puedes venir el sábado.»

answer.text: Lemme know if you can come on Saturday

feedback.es: Lemme know + if introduce la petición de aviso; on Saturday cierra el mensaje con el día.

hint.es: Empieza por la forma reducida de let me.

prompt.es: Leo entendió «seven». ¿Qué palabra debe enfatizar Mia para corregirlo?

choices.text: concert
starts
thirty

feedback.es: El malentendido está en la hora: enfatizar thirty corrige la cifra que Leo no captó.

origin.text: Mia's draft: 'The concert starts at seven thirty, not at seven, so don't be there early.'

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Mia y elige qué espera ella de Sara.

choices.text: That she starts and keeps Mia informed about the menu.
That she waits for Mia at the bus stop.
That she chooses a cheap restaurant for everyone.

feedback.es: Mia pide que empiecen sin ella y que le cuente lo que deciden; lo de la comida barata es solo un comentario suyo.

origin.audio: Hi Sara, it's Mia. I'm gonna be late, because my bus is delayed, so I'll arrive at ten. Please start without me, and lemme know what you decide about the menu. I don't mind which restaurant we pick, as long as there's something cheap to eat.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada bloque del mensaje con su función.

feedback.es: Un mensaje claro encadena identificación, razón, petición y promesa, cada una en su propio bloque.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con los bloques de sentido mejor marcados para una nota de voz.

choices.text: Hi Leo, I'm Mia, the train / leaves at ten, we meet at nine / thirty in front of the station, bring / fifty pounds for the tickets.
Hi Leo, / I'm Mia. / The train leaves at ten, / so we meet at nine thirty / in front of the station. / Bring fifty pounds for the tickets, / and if it rains, / we'll go to the museum instead.
Hi Leo, I'm Mia. The train leaves at ten, so we meet at nine thirty in front of the station. Bring fifty pounds / for the tickets and if it rains we go to the museum instead.

feedback.es: Solo esta versión agrupa cada idea (saludo, hora, lugar, dinero, plan B) y da a cada una su pausa.

origin.text: Draft: Hi Leo I'm Mia the train leaves at ten we meet at nine thirty in front of the station bring fifty pounds for the tickets and if it rains we go to the museum instead.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Mia y elige qué actitud muestra ante el precio.

choices.text: She insists that Leo must pay his share, whatever the cost.
She thinks the tickets are actually cheap for such a good band.
She admits it is costly but leaves him room to say no.

feedback.es: Reconoce que es caro («kinda expensive») y añade «no pressure»: le deja margen para rechazar.

origin.audio: Hi Leo, it's Mia. Listen, I gotta buy the tickets first, so lemme know if you can bring the money. I know it's kinda expensive, about fifty pounds each, but it's a great band, and they hardly ever play here. No pressure, though: if it's too much for you this month, we'll find something cheaper, or I can tell the others we'll go another time. Anyway, call me back when you can.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Devuélveme la llamada en cuanto recibas este mensaje.»

answer.text: Call me back as soon as you get this message

feedback.es: El pronombre va entre call y back, y as soon as + get this message cierra la petición.

prompt.es: Escribe un mensaje de voz para Leo con pausas (/) y dos formas reducidas.

answer.text: Hi Leo, / it's Mia. / I'm gonna be at the station / on SATURDAY / at half past NINE. / We wanna catch the ten o'clock train, / so please don't be late. / I gotta buy the tickets first, / so lemme know / if you can bring the money. / They're kinda expensive, / FIFTY pounds each. / If it rains, / we'll go to the museum instead. / I'll wait for you at the entrance, / and I'll keep my phone on. / Call me back / when you get this, / and send me a message too. / It's gonna be a great day! / See you on Saturday!
accepted: Hi Leo, / it's Mia. / I'm gonna be at the station / on SATURDAY / at half past NINE. / We wanna catch the ten o'clock train, / so please don't be late. / I gotta buy the tickets first, / so lemme know / if you can bring the money. / They're kinda expensive, / FIFTY pounds each. / If it rains, / we'll go to the museum instead. / I'll wait for you at the entrance, / and I'll keep my phone on. / Call me back / when you get this, / and send me a message too. / It's gonna be a great day! / See you on Saturday!

Hey Leo, / it's Mia. / I'm gonna meet you at the station / at nine thirty / on SATURDAY. / The train leaves at ten, / so don't be late. / I gotta buy the tickets, / and they're fifty pounds each, / so please bring the money. / If it rains, / we're gonna go to the museum instead. / Lemme know / if that works for you. / I'll wait for you at the entrance, / and I'll keep my phone on. / It's gonna be a great day, / so please call me back / when you get this. / See you there!

Hi Leo, / Mia here. / See you at the station / on Saturday / at 9:30. / We wanna get the ten o'clock train, / so be on time. / I gotta get the tickets. / They're kinda expensive, / 50 pounds each, / so bring some money. / If it rains, / we'll visit the museum instead. / I'll wait for you at the entrance / and keep my phone on. / It's gonna be a great day, / so call me back / when you hear this, / and send me a message too!

feedback.es: Un buen guion marca bloques con /, acentúa las palabras clave (hora, precio) y usa al menos dos formas reducidas con todos los datos.

origin.text: Datos: Leo y tú quedan el sábado a las 9:30 en la estación; el tren sale a las 10; las entradas cuestan 50 libras cada una y las compras tú; si llueve, irán al museo. Marca las pausas con / y las palabras acentuadas en MAYÚSCULAS.

prompt.es: Completa: el ritmo del inglés depende de acentos a intervalos regulares.

feedback.es: Rhythm es el sustantivo para el patrón de acentos y pausas que hace natural el habla.

origin.text: A message read without pauses is hard to follow. Natural English ___ depends on stressed syllables arriving at regular intervals, not on every single word.

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto producen «gotta» y «lemme» en este mensaje a un cliente?

choices.text: They sound friendly but may be too casual for a business message.
They sound correct and professional with any client.
They show that Mia treats the change as unimportant.

feedback.es: Las formas reducidas dan cercanía, pero en un mensaje profesional a un cliente pueden resultar demasiado informales.

origin.text: Voice note to a client: 'Hi Mr Hale, it's Mia from the agency. I'm afraid I gotta move our meeting. Lemme know what works, and sorry for the trouble!'

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Ana y elige por qué pide a Tom que llegue antes de las ocho.

choices.text: To bring the cake before anyone else arrives.
To help her get everything ready for the party.
To greet the other guests when they arrive.

feedback.es: Ana pide llegar a las siete y media «to help me set up»: ayudar a preparar la fiesta.

origin.audio: Hi Tom. It's Ana. I've already got the cake, so don't buy one. Just bring some drinks, and maybe ice, because the party's gonna be hot. It starts at eight, but come at seven thirty if you can, to help me set up.
